quote: In this initial part, we’ll cover the basics: setting up the project, designing the panel layout, and adding essential controls.

series_key: creating an interactive graphical user interface in mql5
mechanism: Full read of Part 2 with Part 1: OnTick refreshes Bid/Ask/Spread labels; OnChartEvent handles close/profit/loss/pending buttons, lot dropdown, edit validation, hover grow, and drag of dropdown. Live quote labels are display plumbing for a trading panel, not a built sensing algorithm for regime/vol/liquidity.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GOLD (XAUUSD) chart examples; AUDUSD position left open when EA on Gold; tick-level OnTick
why_new_for_mis: After full read this is interactive GUI/trade-panel automation, not a new MIS sensing idea.
quote: Finally, we will update the price quotes to real-time values on every price tick.

mechanism: SpreadMonitor custom indicator: long OnCalculate reads the spread[] timeseries into a DRAW_COLOR_HISTOGRAM; for each bar, if currentSpread > previousSpread color index=1 (clrTomato), else 0 (clrDarkBlue). Visualizes floating-spread spikes and compressions over time.
data_needed: OnCalculate spread[] array; 2 buffers (data + INDICATOR_COLOR_INDEX); rates_total>=2
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPJPY M5 example chart; any floating-spread symbol/PERIOD_CURRENT
why_new_for_mis: Turns broker spread itself into a first-class colored liquidity/cost sensor—MIS can track spread expansion vs compression as a liquidity-stress channel.
quote: When the current spread is higher than the previous spread, the histogram will change to a red color to signify an increase in the spread, and when the current spread is lower than the previous spread the histogram will change to a blue color

mechanism: SmoothedCandlesticks: iMA MODE_SMMA colors DRAW_COLOR_CANDLES—if open, high, low, and close all > SMMA → bull (clrDodgerBlue); all four < SMMA → bear (clrTomato); else grey (MA touches body). Overlays SMMA line; filters noise into a three-state trend regime.
data_needed: iMA(PERIOD_CURRENT, _maPeriod, MODE_SMMA, applied price); OHLC buffers; candleColorBuffer
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any Symbol/PERIOD_CURRENT; default SMMA period 50; chart or separate window
why_new_for_mis: Strict all-extremes-vs-SMMA tristate (bull/bear/neutral) candle regime is a clean MIS visual regime label beyond simple close-vs-MA.
quote: The candles turn green when the open, high, low, and close prices are higher than the smoothed moving average and turn red when the open, high, low, and close prices are lower than the smoothed moving average.

mechanism: LinearMovingAverageHistogram: GetLWMA fills maHistogramBuffer as linear-weighted MA of applied price and priceLineBuffer as current price; DRAW_HISTOGRAM + DRAW_LINE in a separate window so LWMA level vs price is sensed visually.
data_needed: Applied price series; _maPeriod/_maShift inputs; 2 indicator buffers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic chart symbol/period; default MA period 50
why_new_for_mis: LWMA-as-histogram paired with live price line is a lightweight trend-level sensor pattern MIS can reuse as a buffer channel.
quote: It will plot a linear weighted moving average as a histogram and a line representing the current price on a separate window below the price chart.

mechanism: Direct multi-step forecasting: for pred_step=1..5, shift Signal by -step, train a separate LightGBMClassifier on OHLC→next-bar bull/bear (Close>Open), export each to ONNX, and in MQL5 run all five models on the prior H1 bar to emit Next[1..5] Buy/Sell comments.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 OHLC (~1000 bars); Signal=1 if Close>Open else 0; five ONNX LightGBM models
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_H1; horizons 1–5 bars; EA comment on chart
why_new_for_mis: Per-horizon specialized classifiers give MIS a multi-horizon directional sensor vector instead of a single next-bar call.
quote: Direct multistep forecasting is a method where separate predictive models are trained for each future timestep you want to predict.

mechanism: Train one LinearRegression (Close_t → Close_{t+1}); at inference, seed with last close and iteratively replace input with each prediction for N steps (e.g. 10). MQL5 draws horizontal TrendCreate lines at each predicted close. Reports ~91% recursive test accuracy vs one-step ~98%.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 Close series; ONNX LR model; NewBar gate; steps=10
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 training; EA tested on H4 chart printing H1-based forecasts
why_new_for_mis: Iterative single-feature close feedback is a minimal recursive path sensor—MIS can compare recursive drift vs direct multi-horizon outputs.
quote: This prediction is then fed back into the model to make the next prediction. This process is repeated until predictions are made for the desired number of future timesteps.

mechanism: create_target shifts Close for future_steps=5 into y; Sequential Dense(256)-Dense(128)-Dense(5) with MSE predicts five future closes in one forward pass from MinMax-scaled OHLC; ONNX + min/max bins in MQL5; R² ~0.85–0.94 per step; chart trendlines for each horizon.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 OHLC; future_steps target columns; MinMaxScaler bins; NN ONNX
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_H1; 5-step multi-output; EA on H4 showing H1 forecasts
why_new_for_mis: Single-pass multi-output close path captures cross-horizon dependence—MIS multi-horizon level sensor without recursive error cascade.
quote: In a multi-output model, the model is trained to produce a vector of predictions in a single pass. This means the model learns to understand the relationships and dependencies between different future timesteps directly.

mechanism: Build sequences (time_step=5) of scaled Open/High/Low; Conv1D(filters=16,kernel=3,causal,strides=2)+MaxPool extracts local patterns, then SimpleRNN/LSTM/GRU(50) models temporal order; softmax buy/sell (Close>Open). Deploy ONNX via CConvNet; trade on D1 features while polling from H4 NewBar. Tested TSLA; CNN+RNN ~90% trade win rate in sample, LSTM~74%, GRU~61%.
data_needed: TSLA D1 OHLC sequences; StandardizationScaler mean/scale bins; ONNX cnn+rnn/lstm/gru
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Tesla (TSLA) D1 training; EA on H4 chart reading PERIOD_D1 CopyRates; time_step=5
why_new_for_mis: CNN→RNN pipeline separates local pattern sensing from temporal memory—MIS hybrid sequence sensor beyond plain MLP or GBDT.
quote: Since CNNs excel at extracting and detecting features from the data, RNNs are exceptional at interpreting these features over time.

mechanism: CatBoostClassifier on EURUSD D1 OHLC plus Day, DayofWeek, DayofYear, Month; target = next-bar Close>Open buy/sell. Ordered boosting / target encoding for categoricals; feature-importance plot shows calendar fields dominate continuous OHLC. ONNX export (floats for MT5); EA predicts_bin/proba each new bar.
data_needed: EURUSD D1 OHLC; calendar fields from bar time; CatBoost ONNX; CollectData.mq5 script
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 training; Strategy Tester 2021–2024 on H4 open-prices modelling
why_new_for_mis: Calendar-aware GBDT signal with explicit categorical dominance is a neural/tabular sensor MIS can use for seasonality-conditioned direction reads.
quote: It seems the CatBoost model considered the categorical variables as the most impactful features to the model's final predicted outcome than continuous variables.

mechanism: Temporal Fusion Transformer (pytorch-forecasting) on EURUSD M15: target=close pct returns; max_encoder_length=24, max_prediction_length=6; time_varying_known_reals (hour/dow/dom/month, RSI, StochRSI, MACD_diff) vs unknown_reals (OHLC, tick_volume, SMA/EMA20, Bollinger bands); QuantileLoss + attention; Optuna hyperparams; bot trades on sign of last predicted return and retrains on schedule.
data_needed: MT5 EURUSD M15 rates; FeatureEngineer indicators; TimeSeriesDataSet; TFT checkpoint
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD TIMEFRAME_M15; lookback 24 / lookahead 6; ~10000 bars; Python bot via MetaTrader5 package
why_new_for_mis: Attention multi-horizon returns with known-future vs unknown feature split plus quantiles gives MIS an interpretable transformer path sensor (levels, calendar, momentum, vol bands).
quote: A Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) is a state-of-the-art, attention-based deep learning model designed for multi-horizon time-series forecasting.

mechanism: FeatureEngineer stacks bollinger_hband/lband with RSI, StochRSI K/D, MACD diff/signal, SMA/EMA20, and calendar fields into the TFT unknown/known real channels so multi-horizon return forecasts are conditioned on explicit volatility envelopes and momentum oscillators.
data_needed: close series; BB window=20/dev=2; RSI/StochRSI 14; MACD 12/26/9; hour/dow/dom/month
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15 feature frame (~9990 rows after concat)
why_new_for_mis: Packages Bollinger envelope + momentum into a transformer-ready volatility/context stack—MIS can reuse the known/unknown split as a sensing schema even without TFT.
